claim_one_line: THE TORUS-LINK CENSUS, SEALED (not yet run; after B1500): which of the simplest G2 cone singularities -- cones over the four homogeneous nearly Kaehler 6-manifolds S^6, S^3 x S^3, CP^3 and the flag manifold F_{1,2}, modulo finite automorphism groups -- have an ADE singular locus that is a cone over a torus, of what ADE type and what shape? Reduction proved at seal: a non-trivial automorphism fixes points or surfaces of the link; single elements find every torus locus; on the equal-rank links (S^6, CP^3, F_{1,2}) no left translation fixes a torus (every fixed component is a maximal-rank orbit with positive Euler characteristic), so tori can come only from S^3 x S^3 and the flag manifold's order-3 twisted automorphisms. Census pinned: every automorphism class of order <= 12 (left translations and their compositions with the J-preserving outer elements), fixed sets by Newton from 400 seeds, topology from the centraliser orbit, torus shapes from the period lattice in the normal metric, full pointwise stabilisers. Banked identity: B1500's hexagonal S^3 x S^3 torus, S^6's great spheres, the structures' J-checks, the lemma on the census's own elements. Sealed: P1 every torus locus A-type (prior ~90%); P2 every torus hexagonal (~80%); P3 per-link read-outs, F_{1,2} carrying one (~70%).
